I've been testing Anthropic Claude's browser control feature for the past week. My honest take so far: It's slow. Watching it click through an interface is not exciting (the gif is ~4X faster 😬). But here's the thing - when I need to figure out an unfamiliar interface from scratch, it's already faster than me. The real win is different, though. Yesterday I was shipping updates to Naoma AI website, and I added a new step to my agent's workflow: before committing any changes, it opens a browser and checks that everything actually works. It does this in the background while I'm on other tasks. Essentially, I got a free QA engineer who never forgets to run the check. Six months ago this would've sounded like sci-fi. Curious how fast this space keeps moving. What's your experience with browser agents so far? And a bigger question - will we even use browsers in 5 years?
